required_fixes: Expand scope from climate-only risks to all material sustainability-related risks and opportunities (or clearly state scope and include opportunities), and link them to effects on cash flows/access to finance/cost of capital over short/medium/long term (IFRS_S1_3_C01, IFRS_S1_17_C01 alignment).
Add explicit identification of the related financial statements (which set, consolidated/parent, period) and confirm the same reporting entity boundary (IFRS_S1_20_C01, IFRS_S1_22_C01).
State that EUR is the presentation currency of the related financial statements (IFRS_S1_24_C01).
Add a statement on consistency of key data/assumptions with those used in the related financial statements (to the extent possible) (IFRS_S1_23_C01).

Describe connections across sustainability disclosures and other general purpose financial reports (eg, financial statements), including cross-references where relevant (IFRS_S1_21_C04; and if cross-referencing is used, comply with IFRS_S1_63_C01).

Include the required 'sources of guidance' disclosures: whether SASB topics/metrics were considered and what other standards/guidance were applied; identify relevant industry guidance used (IFRS_S1_55_C01, IFRS_S1_58_C01, IFRS_S1_59_C01, IFRS_S1_59_C02).
Add disclosures on significant judgements (non-estimation) made in preparing the sustainability disclosures (IFRS_S1_74_C01).
Strengthen measurement uncertainty disclosures by identifying high-uncertainty amounts and describing sources of uncertainty for each (IFRS_S1_78_C01, IFRS_S1_78_C03).
State whether sustainability disclosures are reported at the same time as the related financial statements (IFRS_S1_64_C01).

Add an explicit statement addressing whether additional information was necessary beyond specifically applicable IFRS SDS requirements to enable users to understand effects on cash flows/access to finance/cost of capital (IFRS_S1_15_C02).

For GR-009, either remove/soften the claim (e.g., 'The disclosures include information intended to help users understand connections...') or add explicit, verifiable linkage evidence in the section (cross-references/mapping showing how governance links to strategy, risk register items, and metrics/targets).

For GR-003, add a brief description of the materiality assessment approach used (process, criteria, governance, and how completeness/neutrality/accuracy were ensured) or rephrase as a policy statement rather than a factual assertion.

For GR-001, clarify what 'presented in EUR' refers to (reporting currency for these sustainability disclosures and/or the financial statements presentation currency) and align wording to the evidenced fields.
For GR-002, if keeping the claim, add a sentence confirming comparatives are prepared on a consistent basis (or disclose any changes in methods/definitions between 2022–2024).

For GR-012, if the section is meant to evidence resilience assessments, include a short, attributable summary of the orderly/disorderly resilience conclusions and key assumptions (or cross-reference where those results are disclosed).

Introduce a short opening paragraph that clearly states the basis of preparation and purpose of the section (e.g., that it explains how sustainability-related financial disclosures are prepared, scoped, and connected to the financial statements).

Convert headings to a numbered hierarchy consistent with the overall report structure (e.g., '1. General requirements', '1.1 Basis of preparation', '1.2 Reporting period and comparatives', '1.3 Fair presentation and material information', '1.4 Connected information', etc.).
Add one-sentence purpose statements at the start of each subsection to explain what is being disclosed and how users should interpret it.

Reframe narrative sentences to use standards-oriented disclosure verbs (e.g., 'We prepare these disclosures for the reporting period ending …', 'We disclose comparative information for …', 'We identify the following climate-related risks as material to our prospects').

Add lead-in sentences before bullet lists that clarify whether the bullets are examples, a subset, or a complete list of items (e.g., 'The climate risk register currently identifies the following material climate-related risks that could reasonably be expected to affect our prospects:').

Clarify and define acronyms and technical terms at first use (e.g., NGFS scenarios, NACE sector classification, EPC energy performance certificates, LTV loan-to-value, CDP disclosure) or add a cross-reference to a definitions/abbreviations section.

Avoid hard-coding specific dates, years, currencies, and jurisdiction lists in template-style narrative; where such specifics are necessary for this report, frame them as report-specific parameters and ensure they are not embedded in reusable boilerplate text.

Expand the 'Basis of preparation' and related subsections to describe alignment with the financial reporting boundary, treatment of estimates and judgements, and how sustainability-related information is connected to the primary financial statements, using cross-reference placeholders where detailed information is provided elsewhere.

Under 'Connected information', restructure content so that Governance, Strategy, Risk Management, and Metrics and Targets are either separate numbered subsections or clearly cross-referenced to their dedicated sections, rather than only appearing as bullets.

Where scenario analysis and resilience assessments are described, clarify whether they relate to the current reporting period and, if they involve estimates or forward-looking assumptions, use cautious modality and briefly note that they are subject to methodological uncertainty.

Add at least one brief closing sentence for the section (or major subsections) that provides connectivity to other parts of the report set (e.g., 'Refer to [Section: Governance] for further detail on board oversight of climate-related risks and opportunities.').

section_generation_score.policy: Missing requirements reduce audit/readiness visibility only; they must not appear in report prose.
